REPUBLIC OF THE PHILIPPINES DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT A. Francisco Gold Condominium II EDSA Cor. Mapagmahal St., Diliman Quezon City LEGAL SERVICE HON. ANDRES D. DANGEROS Municipal Vice-Mayor Municipality of Sablayan Province of Occidental Mindoro Dear Vice Mayor Dangeros: DILG Legal Opinion No. 93 s. 2011 DEC 05 2011 This has reference to your 26 October 2011 letter which requests the Department's opinion on whether the soft loan extended by the Municipality of Sablayan to Occidental Mindoro Electric Cooperative, Inc. (OMECO), a local electric cooperative, may be charged against the Municipality's balances of the calamity fund for CY 2010. Based on your narration, the Municipality of Sablayan has suffered from unstable power supply and iow power reliability due to its dependence to the 69kV power lines from Calapan, Oriental Mindoro. This prompted said LGU to seek the assistance of the NAPOCOR and the DOE to mitigate the problem. The NAPOCOR proposed the establishment of a power substation in Barangay Malisbong, Sablayan which was agreed to by said municipality considering that it is the best alternative to resolve the perennial issue. The Municipal Mayor and the Sangguniang Bayan then agreed to extend a soft loan to OMECO for the purchase of step up transformer to be put up in the proposed substation. Hence, this query. Based on the foregoing, we opine that the municipality's unstable power supply and low power reliability does not constitute as a disaster as defined under RA 10121, viz: "Disaster" - a serious disruption of the functioning of a community or a society involving widespread human, material, economic or environmental losses and impacts, which exceeds the ability of the affected community or society to cope using its own resources. Disasters are often described as a result of the combination of: the exposure to hazard; the conditions of vulnerability that are present; and insufficient capacity or measures to reduce or cope with the potential negative consequences. Disasters may include loss of life, injury, disease and other negative effects on human, physical, mental and social well being, together with damage to property, destruction of assets, loss of services, social and economic disruption and environmental degradation. The unstable power supply in said municipality is not the type of "disaster" contemplated under RA 10121. Furthermore, it does not entail a serious disruption of the functioning of the community as a consequence of a widespread hurnan, material, economic or environmental losses and impacts, which exceeds the ability of the Municipality of Sablayan, Occidental Mindoro and its constituency to cope using its own resources. It must be borne in mind that pursuant to Section 21 of RA 10121, the Local Disaster Risk Reduction Management Fund (LDRRMF), which was formerly known as "calamity fund", should be used to support disaster risk management activities such as, but not limited to pre-disaster preparedness programs including training, purchasing life- saving rescue equipment, supplies and medicines, for post disaster activities, for the payment of premiums on calamity insurance and construction of evacuation centers. A "post disaster recovery" as defined under Section 3 (aa) of RA 10121 is "the restoration and improvement where appropriate, of faci/ities, /ive/ihood and living conditions of disaster-affected communities, including efforts to reduce disaster risk factors, in accordance with the princip/es of "build back better

Hence, even assuming arguendo that the unstable power supply of the Municipality of Sablayan is a "disaster", the proposed loan extension of the municipality to OMECO does not fall within the purview of the "post disaster recovery" contemplated by RA 10121. We hope to have enlightened you on the foregoing. Very truly yours, JE US DO Director 111 LS08:rb
